medical-llm.notes:
I verified 13 references. All of them come from the requested list apart from Tian et al. 2024, which I added as a peer-reviewed survey because Kim et al. 2025 has no journal version.

How I checked them:
- Each DOI's metadata came from Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/<doi>).
- Journal articles were cross-checked against Europe PMC records (abstract, PMID, PMCID).
- ACL papers were opened on ACL Anthology.
- JAMA Internal Medicine and the OUP Briefings in Bioinformatics page were opened directly.
- arXiv IDs were confirmed through the arXiv API.
- PubMed and PMC pages returned cookie or reCAPTCHA walls, and NEJM AI returned 403. For those I used Crossref and Europe PMC instead, and the source_checked field gives the URL I actually opened.
- Author lists longer than 6 are cut to the first 6 plus "et al." as the schema asks.

Caveats:
1. **Kim et al. 2025 is a preprint only.** There is no peer-reviewed version as of now. The arXiv v2 (2 Nov 2025) title says "Medical Hallucinations…" (plural), while the medRxiv version says "Medical Hallucination…". Crossref's medRxiv record lists "Shen Chen" where arXiv lists "Shan Chen". I cited arXiv v2 and used its arXiv DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2503.05777.
2. **Almanac's numbers changed between versions.** The NEJM AI version's evaluation (314 questions, 9 specialties, 8 clinicians plus 2 practitioners) differs from the earlier arXiv/PMC version (130 scenarios). My summary uses the NEJM AI numbers. Crossref's title uses an em dash ("Almanac — Retrieval-Augmented…"). NEJM AI has no page numbers, so the pages field holds the article ID AIoa2300068.
3. **Tian et al. year.** Europe PMC and Crossref print date say 2023 (online 22 Nov 2023). The OUP page gives Vol 25, Issue 1, January 2024, published 2 Jan 2024, so I used 2024.
4. **Med-PaLM 2 is cited as Nature Medicine 2025.** That is 31(3):943-950, published online 8 Jan 2025. The arXiv title differs slightly: "Towards Expert-Level…".
5. **SourceCheckup's arXiv title differs from the journal title.** arXiv 2402.02008 is titled "How well do LLMs cite relevant medical references? An evaluation framework and analyses"; I cite the Nature Communications title.
6. **Med-HALT venue name.** The CoNLL venue is "Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning" (Anthology and Crossref). Some web summaries wrongly say "Processing".
7. **Omiye et al. was picked for the "npj Digital Medicine safety/bias" item.** It is the race-based medicine paper.

Row-by-row results:

(2) npj Digital Medicine 2025 -> Asgari et al. 2025, npj Digit Med 8:274. High. Hallucinations persist even when the source transcript is given (1.47%, of which 44% were major).
(3) Authorea 2025 -> LOW confidence, unresolved. I searched Crossref (Authorea prefix 10.22541 and TechRxiv prefix 10.36227, posted 2025) and the web with many keyword sets. No 2025 Authorea preprint on medical RAG safety or verification turned up. The only close match is Jubair, 'RAG vs. Fine-Tuning: A Systematic Review of Hallucination Mitigation in Medical LLMs', Authorea, but it was posted 21 Jan 2026. The topic fits; the year does not. I included it flagged low, but it should not be cited as "Authorea 2025" unless the team confirms it.
(4) CMC 2025 -> Geng, Xu, Qu & Wong, CMC 87(1), Article 4. Medium. The DOI is 10.32604/cmc.2025.074081 and it was accepted Nov 2025, but the issue is dated 2026, so the reference must say 2026. It is a survey that explicitly discusses structural instruction/data separation defenses (StruQ, spotlighting). The other CMC 2025 candidate (Ergün & Onan, adversarial prompt detection, 10.32604/cmc.2025.063826) is about classifier-based detection, not isolation, so I rejected it.
(5) ACL Findings 2025 -> MedCite (Wang et al.), Findings ACL 2025, pp. 18891–18913. High.
(6) ACL/EMNLP Findings 2024 -> Chen et al., 'Controlling Risk of Retrieval-augmented Generation: A Counterfactual Prompting Framework', Findings EMNLP 2024, pp. 2380–2393. High. C-RAG (Kang et al.) is ICML 2024, not ACL/EMNLP; it is added only as a supplementary reference.

retrieval-ml.notes:
I verified all 16 references from primary or registry pages: Crossref, ACL Anthology, the NeurIPS proceedings site (with its BibTeX), the arXiv API, GitHub and the official websites. I did not make up any DOIs. MiniLM (NeurIPS 2020) and DeBERTaV3 (ICLR 2023) have no publisher DOI, so their doi field is empty. For arXiv-only items I used the DOI that arXiv issues (10.48550/arXiv.<id>).

Things the author should know:

1. **BM25 (Robertson & Zaragoza):** the volume and pages conflict between sources.
   - The authors' own PDF (staff.city.ac.uk) prints "Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval, Vol. 3, No. 4 (2009) 333–389, DOI 10.1561/1500000019". I used this, and it is the citation everyone uses.
   - The current Crossref record, now hosted by Emerald after it took over Now Publishers, says vol. 4, issue 1–2, pp. 1–174. That looks like a re-registration error. The DOI is the same in both.

2. **Sentence-BERT pages:** ACL Anthology says pp. 3982–3992 and Crossref says 3980–3990. I used the ACL Anthology numbers because it is the publisher.

3. **DeBERTaV3 venue:** ICLR 2023 is confirmed by the arXiv comments field ("published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023"). The OpenReview page sits behind a browser check I could not pass, so the url points to arXiv. I did not verify the OpenReview forum id, so I left it out.

4. **Long author lists:** these follow the rule of listing the first 6 authors, then "et al.".
   - DPR has 8 authors. The last two are Danqi Chen and Wen-tau Yih.
   - Qwen3 lists 60 authors on arXiv, starting with An Yang.
   - Gemma 3 lists 216, starting with "Gemma Team". In IEEE style it can simply be cited as "Gemma Team et al.".

5. **SummaC arXiv id:** the correct id is 2111.09525. Note that 2111.09452 is an unrelated paper.

6. **"Lin et al. hybrid retrieval":** I included both SPLADE (Formal et al., SIGIR 2021) and Ma, Sun, Pradeep, Li & Lin (ECIR 2022), which is the paper showing dense+BM25 hybrids are stronger than DPR reported.
   - DOI, pages 613–626 and ISBN come from Crossref.
   - The LNCS volume, 13185 (ECIR 2022 Part I, eBook ISBN 978-3-030-99736-6), comes from the Springer book listing as surfaced in search. Springer's own page redirected to a login and Crossref has no volume field, so check it before final typesetting.

7. **C-Pack:** the BGE embedding models were introduced in this paper, so cite it as the BGE source. If MedBridge uses BGE-M3 specifically, that model comes from a separate paper (Chen et al. 2024, "M3-Embedding") that I have not checked.

8. **Ollama and Qdrant:** these are software references.
   - The release versions shown (Ollama v0.40.2, Qdrant v1.19.2) were the latest on GitHub on 2026-10-09. Replace them with the versions MedBridge actually runs, and add "accessed 2026-10-09" in IEEE style.
   - The licences are MIT for Ollama and Apache-2.0 for Qdrant. Qdrant's site advertises native dense+sparse hybrid search.

9. **Cross-encoder model card:** if the report names the exact reranker or NLI checkpoint (for example cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 or a DeBERTa-v3 NLI cross-encoder on Hugging Face), add the model card as a web reference. I did not verify any model cards.

10. **Sources I could not open directly:** the ACM DL, Now Publishers/Emerald, Springer, DBLP and OpenReview pages returned 403s or bot-challenges. I verified those papers through the Crossref API, the authors' own copies and arXiv instead.

(2) Landis & Koch 1977: Crossref gives only the first page (159). The page range 159-174 comes from PubMed (PMID 843571).

(3) Efron & Tibshirani: the print edition is Chapman & Hall, New York, 1993 (Open Library: ISBN 0412042312, Monographs on Statistics and Applied Probability 57, xvi+436 pp). The DOI 10.1201/9780429246593 is the Chapman and Hall/CRC ebook record, which Crossref dates 1994-05-15. Cite year 1993 and, if you want, keep the DOI.

(4) NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 was WITHDRAWN on 26 Sept 2025 and replaced by Rev. 2, so I returned Rev. 2 instead. Rev. 1 metadata, if needed: "Guidelines for Media Sanitization", Richard Kissel, Andrew Regenscheid, Matthew Scholl, Kevin Stine, December 2014, DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-88r1.

(5) EU AI Act: according to Publications Office metadata, it was amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (the "Digital Omnibus on AI", published 24 July 2026). A consolidated version dated 27 July 2026 exists. I did not open the 2026/1744 text, so I cannot say exactly what it changes (it likely includes the timing of high-risk obligations). The report should cite 2024/1689 and add "as amended". EUR-Lex itself blocked automated fetches, so the title, date and ELI were checked from the Cellar notice and the full Official Journal text. The de-identification page was last reviewed 22 Aug 2024, and its PDF is dated 26 Nov 2012 and lists identifiers (A)-(R). The url fields hold the live HHS URLs.
